title: Leaf collapse retracts fixed-word tree zigzag categories
statement: Let $T$ be a small oriented tree: its underlying undirected graph is nonempty and has a unique finite simple path between any two vertices, and each edge is assigned one direction. Let $C_T$ be its free path category, whose arrows are finite composable directed edge words and whose identities are empty words. For a finite word $w$ in $+,-$, let $Z_w^{C_T}(x,y)$ have the meaning of [def-coef-zigzag-homotopy-calculus] for the pair $(C_T,C_T)$; identity horizontal arrows are allowed. Let $l$ be a leaf (a vertex incident to exactly one undirected edge), $a$ its neighbour, and $x,y$ vertices different from $l$. Put $T\prime=T\setminus\{l\}$, deleting also its incident edge. The inclusion $i:C_{T\prime}\to C_T$ and the functor $r:C_T\to C_{T\prime}$ sending $l$ to $a$, its incident edge to $1_a$, and all other vertices and generating edges to themselves induce functors $I_w:Z_w^{C_{T\prime}}(x,y)\to Z_w^{C_T}(x,y)$ and $R_w$ in the reverse direction. They satisfy $R_wI_w=1$. If the incident edge points $l\to a$, there is a natural transformation $1\Rightarrow I_wR_w$; if it points $a\to l$, there is a natural transformation $I_wR_w\Rightarrow1$. Its component at a zigzag has the incident edge at every occurrence of $l$ and identities at all other vertices; in particular its endpoint components are identities.
